title: Relaxed (passive) trunk moment-angle in flexion, extension and lateral bend: exponential fit

quantity.name: applied moment about L4/L5 vs normalised trunk angle
quantity.definition: exponential least-squares fit M = k exp(d*phi) to pooled trials and subjects; M = applied moment at L4/L5 (Nm), phi = trunk angle as % of max standing RoM; stiffness K = k d exp(d*phi) (Nm/%RoM). Moment-angle points given at 0-100% are computed from the fit (derived)

protocol.summary: Hips, knees and ankles secured on a fixed lower-body platform; upper body (arms, torso, shoulders) secured in a cradle gliding on nylon ball bearings over plexiglass (frictionless); right side-lying for flexion/extension, supine for right lateral bend. Experimenter pulled a cable perpendicular to the cradle at ~4-6 deg/s until no further rotation possible. Moment = force x moment arm from force application to the L4/L5 level. Angle: Isotrak source over sacrum and sensor over T12 (flexion/extension), source below ASIS level on lower abdomen and sensor over xiphoid (lateral bend); angle normalised to % of max RoM measured from upright standing. Relaxed = 'minimal activation' instruction; braced = abdominal co-activation to ~5/10/15% MVC at a right external-oblique biofeedback site; 14 EMG channels checked post hoc; 3 trials per condition, data pooled across trials and subjects.
how_to_simulate: Posture: side-lying (flexion/extension) or supine (lateral bend), hips/knees/ankles fixed, upper body on a frictionless cradle (no gravity moment in the plane of motion)
Impose lumbar flexion, extension or right lateral bend from neutral up to the model's maximum standing RoM; express angle as % of that max
Set all muscle activations to zero (passive muscle force-length only) and compute the passive resisting moment about L4/L5 (= applied moment)
Compare M at each %RoM with the fitted curve; compare stiffness slope (Nm/%RoM)
protocol.notes: Fit pooled across subjects/trials (no between-subject SD). The extension curve has a large intercept k (12 Nm at 0%), i.e. a moment was needed to initiate motion. Max standing RoM values and peak moments are in Figs 5-7 (not digitised). Relaxed condition counts as passive.

pass_rule.rule: model moment within +- fit RMS error of the fitted curve at 20-100 %RoM
